verses.text: For the music director, to the tune of “The Lilies of the Covenant.” A psalm by Asaph. Hear us, Shepherd of Israel. You lead Joseph like a flock. You sit above the cherubim. Shine out!
Show your strength before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh. Come save us!
Bring us back, God. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
LORD God of Armies, how long will your anger burn against your people’s prayers?
You’ve fed them bread made of tears and given them tears to drink by the bowlful.
You’ve made our neighbors fight over us, and our enemies laugh among themselves.
Bring us back, God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt. You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it. It sank its roots deep and filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, and its branches were like God’s cedars.
It spread its branches all the way to the sea and sent its shoots out to the River.
Why did you break down its walls so anyone walking by can pick from it?
Wild boars from the woods tear it up, and animals from the fields feed on it.
Come back, God of Armies, please. Look down from heaven. See what’s happened and come care for this vine,
the root your right hand planted, the branch you made strong for yourself.
It’s been burned and cut down. At your rebuke they perish.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, the son of man you made strong for yourself.
Then we won’t turn away from you. Bring us back to life and we’ll call on your name.
Bring us back, LORD God of Armies. Let your face shine on us, and we’ll be saved.
